english.title: Carrier - vehicle carrying dangerous / pressurised goods - carriage of goods in a tank when prohibited

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) was the carrier of goods or equipment subject to the Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009, namely **(..SPECIFY THE CHARACTER OF THE GOODS / EQUIPMENT..), which were in a vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), and the carriage of such goods or equipment in a tank was prohibited by the European Agreement concerning the International Carriage of Dangerous Goods by Road (ADR) 3.2
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 5 of the Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009 and section 33(1)(c) and (3) of the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.

english.notes:
This CJS Code and Standard offence Wording document made OBSOLETE as of 29/02/2012.

(i) For further guidance see the prosecution guide.
(ii) In the first instance a prohibition notice under section 22 of the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 should be applied in accordance with HSE policy. Failure to comply with that prohibition should result in prosecution. Care should however be taken to obtain evidence to prove that the operator in the interim period had not complied with and therefore discharged the prohibition notice.
(iii) Where there is evidence of multiple offences, blatant disregard of the regulations or there has been previous advice, prosecution should also be considered.
(iv) ADR 2009 section 7.1 refers.
